title: repr() of message parts raises ValueError when a field holds a numpy array
author: otiscuilei

comments.author: pydanty[bot]
comments.body:
<!-- pydanty:status-comment:v1 -->

## pydanty status: bug -- confirmed (high), signal 6/10 - p:3-mid

**Why:** `repr()` should never raise. This bug crashes `repr(part)`, `print(result.all_messages())`, logging, and traceback formatting whenever a tool returns a numpy array or pandas object — a common case in data/analysis agents. It can turn an unrelated error into a confusing secondary crash during traceback formatting. The fix is in a shared helper used by many public message-part dataclasses, so all benefit from one change.
**Evidence:** code_librarian confirmed the exact implementation of `dataclasses_no_defaults_repr` at _utils.py:541 — it uses `if f.repr and getattr(self, f.name) != f.default` with no try/except and no special handling for required fields. `ToolReturnPart.content` is a required field (`f.default is dataclasses.MISSING`), and `ToolReturnPart` inherits `__repr__ = _utils.dataclasses_no_defaults_repr` from `BaseToolReturnPart` (messages.py:1449). reproducer confirmed all three claims: (1) `repr(ToolReturnPart(tool_name='t', content=np.array([1,2,3])))` raises ValueError; (2) a pure-Python stand-in class with `__ne__` returning non-bool with exploding `__bool__` also triggers the crash — no numpy needed for tests; (3) `repr(ModelRequest(parts=[part]))` propagates the same crash. No existing tests for `dataclasses_no_defaults_repr` were found.
**Playground:** https://play.pydantic.work/p/cPARTcJu
**Next:** pr_ready -- Confirmed localized bug: `dataclasses_no_defaults_repr` crashes on non-bool `!=` results. Fix is narrow and backwards-compatible.
